newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUISENBERG FAVOURS FLEXIBILITY ON EMU - RADIO.
newsitem.headline: DUISENBERG FAVOURS FLEXIBILITY ON EMU - RADIO.

text.p: Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg would prefer a flexible interpretation of the entry criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU) rather than a delay in the January 1999 launch date, Dutch radio reported on Wednesday.

Officials at the central bank were not immediately available to comment on the report which appeared at odds with public statements by Duisenberg and other top Dutch public officials in which they have consistently called for strict interpretation of the EMU criteria.

NOS radio news said Duisenberg, who is set to take over in July as head of the European Monetary Institute -- the forerunner of the European Central Bank -- had made his remarks at a closed meeting of members of parliament for Prime Minister Wim Kok's Labour Party (PvdA) two weeks ago.

It said leading Labour member of parliament Jacques Wallage had confirmed that Duisenberg discussed EMU with the party and had said at the time that the Maastricht Treaty did not insist EMU members should meet the target figures for entry exactly, as long as they had made good progress towards attaining them.
The EMU entry criteria include a ceiling of three percent of gross domestic product for national public sector deficits.
